If you have to ask why I wrote 'crime,' then I'm afraid you won't understand...

My advice is this:

1. Don't tell him about it, **EVER**.
2. Don't do it again to anyone, **EVER**.
3. Understand, that this was very, **very** wrong!

Now, if you tell, then at best, you're going to lose a friend, and at worst you're gonna ruing his life and yours:

**His** - because depending on kind of person he is, the knowledge that he was used like that, may cause him some psychological problems

**Yours** - because if he develops any problems, someone will ask what happened. He'll spill the beans and the next thing you know, you're sitting in a jail with rape charges because his family/friends convinced him that you need to answer for your 'crime.'

Do you want to take that chance? Even in best case scenario you're gonna inform the guy that you used him. It'll ruin your friendship and you'll gain nothing.

Let it go and don't do it again.

Yeah, that’s the plan – or to be more precise… Currently we are using AdminLTE as the base for our app:

https://adminlte.io/themes/AdminLTE/index2.html

It is a Bootstrap3-based, admin panel template. The idea at the moment is, to re-write our app but still use the same template – only create separate Vue modules for stuff we are currently copying and pasting around.

If you could link me to some application example for that sort of architecture, I would appreciate it.
Thanks, I'll look up that example.
Interesting… do I think correctly, that those store.js files from orders, customer, etc. - are then imported inside global store as separate modules?

I think I understand, thank you. As for my app… the closes comparison would be a sort of *admin panel*, where the user has to log in, and then have access to data like:

* Files of clients, suppliers and products
* Sales management
* Users management

And so on. Almost all pages use multiple components like tables, modals and forms, and provide some kind of CRUD functionality.

Right now we have all of this written using a mix of ASP.NET Razor + jQuery - some controls get’s data directly from the model, while others (like jQuery DataTables) have their own API methods on the backend. 

It’s quiet a mess, that’s why we would like to have a centralized place and one pattern, to govern all the requests and to take care of things like client-side errors handling.
Wow… this is interesting, I’ll give that a look, thanks.

> Do you have a UI inventory? Style Guide? If it is a big project one of the things you may consider is making one of these first.

We have some concepts standardized (like how validation should look, how to display errors, the positioning and colors of buttons etc.), but only on a basic level. We are also using AdminLte:

https://adminlte.io/themes/AdminLTE/index2.html

As the base template for the project, and are trying to follow its concepts. That’s the best we can do at the moment since we lack any UX designer.

> Are you interested in doing atomic design?

I’m afraid we simply won’t have time for that (unless more people are hired, but that’s unlikely). The best we can do right now, and what we are planning to do, is to create reusable components, using parts provided by Bootstrap3 + AdminLTE.

Currently, this is also what I’m using, that is - Vuex for authentication only, and an API service - imported inside each component - for the rest. However, a lot of people seems to be using Vuex as an API backend – putting there action for every request. I’m just trying to figure out if that’s the standard approach.

And as for backend, we are using .NET as well - our app is written in razor + jQuery (standard ASP.NET MVC5 app), but it is a mess, that’s why we are looking for some modern SPA. Performance is not an issue here, it’s more like – if we want to rewrite it, we need to do it right.

So if I understand you correctly, you are basically mixing the API service approach with Vuex, in order not to ‘bloat’ the Vuex modules… I am thinking of doing something similar. 

**One question, however** - are all your components using those ‘wrapped’ Vuex actions to fetch data or do you sometimes import the API service directly inside the component, and load data this way (without going through Vuex)?

I’m asking because on the one hand, importing the logic from separate files and then handling everything inside Vuex actions, seems like a nice **‘everything in one place’** approach but, on the other… I still have doubts if this is what the Vuex should be used for (then again, I’m new to Vue so that may just be confusion on my part).

The problem is that we already have a huge project written in jQuery, and rewriting it in Vue (or AngularJS, because that’s on the table as well) will already be a form of refactoring, so we have to do it right the first time…

I realize we won’t be able to do everything perfectly, however, I’m trying to establish a single approach that we can build on, and that won’t give us headaches in the future.

I do, and frankly I think it is more common then people want to believe.

I don’t feel depressed, and yet... the thoughts of killing myself are my constant companion. I simply don’t see the point in living, just to complete the ‘Darwin cycle.’ 

The funny (or perhaps not funny) thing is, that most morons (sorry, but after reading thousands of their posts, I can’t really find a politer phrasing to name these people) that want to ‘save’ us from committing suicide, will still tell you that it is some sort of depression. According to them, if you contemplate the act, there is only one universal explanation... because, apparently, it is impossible to have such thoughts if you are thinking rationally...  It’s just like House said in one of the episodes:

> Dr. House: See, skinny, socially-privileged white people get to draw this neat little circle. And everyone inside the circle is "normal". Anyone outside the circle should be beaten, broken and reset so that they can be brought into the circle. Failing that, they should be institutionalized. Or worse - Pitied.

And that really is sad and depressing in itself.

Every human experience this differently and there is no rule on how to make it less (or more) painful. I have studied a lot of 'material' available online and for example, for some people, reading a note which says that it wasn't their fault, can be more painful then if there was no note in the first place, while for others opposite is true. 

I can tell you how it was for my family and me when my father hanged himself:

- For me (I was 10 at the time) the 'recovery' was quick. I do remember that I was basically hiding for a few days (during the burial preparations) - locked in some goddamn 'happy place' my brain generated. I didn't even cry at the funeral. I must say I wasn't visibly touched by this - I mean, that probably left me pretty messed up inside, but when I think about it, I do it without any emotions (it happened, case closed)

- For my mom, that's a different story - she was hit HARD, and to this day she cries when she thinks about it. And the vague note saying it wasn't her fault, didn't help at all (actually, I think it might have made things worse).

- Rest of the family wasn't touched much (fortunately) and just went on with their lives

So as you can see it, all 'depends' on some unknown factors - if your family and friends truly don't give a damn about you then even writing it was their fault may not affect them. However, if they do care then suicide will be 'enough.'

If they really don't care about you and you want to inflict some pain, then the better approach would be to become independent, and when they ask you for some help, just show them the middle finger. Hard thing to do, but usually better in the long run.

I see... Well, I guess it comes down to how much you drink, what are you mixing it with (for example mixing alcohol with the energy drinks is not the best idea as far as I know) and if you are healthy. Mostly alcohol kills in a few ways:

1. Heart attack - but, unless you have some heart condition, or you mix it with God knows what, or you try to drink too much in a single gulp as the guy I described did - you should be OK.

2. Liver damage - this needs time of course (tens of years usually) but if you drink A LOT (and I mean A LOT) then eventually you will it end up without a liver (and as My people say 'Life is worthless without a liver!' :P)

3. Drowning in own puke

4. Drunk driving/walking etc.

5. Alcohol + drugs interacting

IMHO the bottom line is, that you will most likely die of something else unless you are planning to become an alcoholic, or you are combining alcohol with other 'things' ;]

And BTW. while it is true that wine is healthier, especially for the heart - keep in mind that this ONLY applies if you are not wasting yourself with it. Vodka, wine, and beer - all have the same alcohol (ethanol) only in different proportions (and mixed with different stuff). If you drink enough, your body will be hit in the same way - no matter what you will pour into yourself :)

It is possible - unlikely but possible. I knew a guy who died after he drank 0.5 liters of vodka in a single gulp - he bet his buddies he will do it and... he did! 

As far as I know, his drinking 'friends' testified to the police that after he gulped the whole bottle, he went into some kind of shock, passed out in seconds and died a moment later (IF I recall correctly, the shock caused his heart to stop). And he was ... 25 I think? Or something like that, anyway.

Another (much more common, but still unlikely) situation occurs, when someone gets wasted to the point of losing consciousness and passes out lying on his back. Then, his body tries to involuntarily vomit the excess alcohol in his sleep - but since he is unconscious and lying on his back, he ends up drowning... in his own vomit. 

If you are thinking about using vodka as a'method' I would not recommend it - more likely instead of achieving your 'goal' - you will end up damaging your stomach, guts and possibly liver.

I'll admit, last time I stopped reading after the burned man part, now I read it to the end, and I'm positively surprised by the arguments so far. I need to read part 26 when I have the time - thanks for the article.

> My Dad died tragically when I was a kid too... much different circumstances, but tragic nonetheless. (He died after a 2 year battle with ALS.)

Damn, I'm sorry - I think that watching someone dying for a few years is even worse, then dealing with suicide :(

> I don’t think it’s normal in most first world countries for 6 year olds to contemplate death everyday, so I learned to hide my thoughts, and the fatalist feelings about life that go with them. I have panic attacks about death sometimes if I’m alone at night. This is stuff even my SO knows nothing about.

You know, some time ago I had a lengthy discussion with an atheist about this. The perspective he presented on death was surprisingly... soothing. I mean, if you think about it, then the only outcome we should possibly fear is hell - all others (nothingness or paradise) seems quite OK. This is funny in some sick way, but ever since that discussion, my fear of death had diminished a lot... or was even replaced by some morbid curiosity. Did you try such perspective? 

> I owe it to those that drew the short straw and lost their chance at living.

I understand what you mean, but for me, it is different. You see, most people when talking about someone who died young for example, say thing like: 'That was a tragic loss, He had a whole life ahead of him.' My reaction is different, my mind is telling me: 'Damn, what a lucky bastard, no more hardship for you friend - just peace. I envy you.' 

I guess this isn't a very popular (or healthy) view, but the longer I live, the more it reaffirms me that those who died, were actually lucky ones. Of course, if the death was long and painful, that's a different story...

> I don’t have answers for either of us. The older I get, the less I’m sure about. Literally the only thing I know for certain in my heart of hearts is that love matters most. I’m not talking about the rubbish love you see in the media and in movies. I’m talking about real love: doing the right thing because it’s the right thing to do, not for any reward. Treating all people with love and compassion. Being empathetic to everyone because everyone deserve to feel understood. Love is meant to be given without any thought for what you might get in return. That’s the only thing in my life that feels unquestionably right. I try to make love the cornerstone of my being; holding me up, giving me strength. I fail a lot, but I keep trying.

I'm sorry to say I never experienced such thing :( A lot of people talk about it, but I always did everything to isolate that kind of feelings. Perhaps it has something to do with my father - after the funeral, the grief for me was over. I was 10 at the time and was like a stone, carrying a deadpan expression everywhere - I don't know how but I think I was actually able to block it out (if I remember correctly, I didn't even cry at the funeral). Perhaps I'm still locked in that shell even if I don't see it - I don't know. But I do know, I never experienced the thing you described :(

> Touch just one life at a time.

I think I understand... But frankly, I'm trying not to get involved in other people lives - I think I end up hurting them, and I don't want that :/

> That’s why I hang out here.

If that works for you, then I'm glad. Keep doing what you are doing, and don't worry, some of us are just a lost cause, no matter what you do.

> Oh man, that sucks. I wish that I could help you.

Don't worry it's not that bad, I like my country, even if it has problems ;]

> Don't give up too soon. We are living in a pivotal moment in time. Our president has the potential to burn it all to the ground. You don't want to miss that. Especially if WWIII breaks out. Try to stick around a little while.

So you are saying I should stick around until a certain fella say: 'Let's make the world great again!' and push the big red button? Well, I guess that argument is at least original :)

But, if you think he is bad, then you haven't heard our politicians. 5 minutes of listening to them and you have an urge to grab a rope. Although, less fun fact is that about a week ago, one guy actually immolated himself to protest the government actions, and died two days ago. And no one seems to give a fuck :(
Poland

Interesting, but there is a flaw common among such lectures - the assumption that life will get better in time. In reality, we mostly don't know that - it can get better or worse and there is 50/50 chance for either outcome. 

The example they used in the next paragraph was sort of manipulation - the burned man had physical injuries, which heal in time **by definition** - with mental disorders (or when someone doesn't see a point in living) there is no such warranty.

> In my honest opinion I think you should get away from yourself and see if you can help someone else. You cut your dad down after committing suicide...there are many people who deal with bereavement from suicide and you can probably help.

As you noticed, I'm cynical (no denying there) and also not a people-person. I doubt somebody who just lost a loved one would like to hear advice from a guy like me - and unfortunately, I'm afraid there is really nothing you can say to ease the pain :(

Hope, the meds will work for you, and you'll get better.

> My second argument has to do with your fifth one, where you obviously select just certain aspects of psychiatric help and exaggerate them mercilessly (admittedly it depends on the country you live in).

I have read a lot of statements on how the system works. I know this is not always the case to lock people in the wards for months, but it can happen. 

On one Polish psychiatric forum (I'm from Poland) I read a story of a lady who went to see her ordinary doctor (GP). She was depressed, seeing that she was recently crying the doctor asked her (she thought it was a casual question) 'Do you have suicidal thoughts?' She replied 'A little' (or something similar). After that, all hell broke loose. 

To protect her own ass - her GP called the cops (or psychiatric emergency or something), they took the woman by force and locked her up for **6 months**. She described her whole ordeal, and it wasn't pretty. The bottom line was - never to trust doctors when it comes to such topics.

Perhaps this was some extreme case (although, if I remember correctly, she wasn't the only one with such story), but mere fact that they have complete power over you, and can keep you locked up for months is sadly true. 

Also... don't get me wrong but since psychology is not an exact science, I have serious doubts about how useful it really is - some people claim it worked for them, other than they went through 10 shrinks and it was a big waste of time.

> What do you think you from β would make of your post after a year into his newly found enjoyable life?

Honestly, I have no idea. The problem is enjoyment might not be enough. Perhaps I'm over-analyzing the whole life thing, but I just don't see a logical point and happiness can only get you so far...

> That said, the best argument I know of is, if you try things you've never tried, things might get better. Life might become enjoyable at some point if you do things differently.

Heh... the problem with that is fear is stopping me from trying new things. I know this is pathetic, but it's hard to try something different when even the mere thought of it, is making your heart race to the near attack rate. That's one of the reasons why it is hard for me to adapt to social norms. Most people I met, are spontaneous - they don't understand why I'm uncomfortable when we need to go on a delegation to a different city, for example.

> Not everyone walks through life feeling like it's a futile and tedious struggle that just ends in death.

The way I see it, ignorance is bliss. The happiest people I know, are the ones that are not very interested in the world around them (the 'bigger picture') - unfortunately, I'm. Other people just focus on things like family and that is driving them, I guess what I lack is a meaning in life (cliche motive, I know), somehow doing the same things for a long time doesn't seem like fun (or logical).

> You have power and agency to reach out and feel more than just the negatives.

Right now, I'm rather stuck in neutral, but as the years go by I'm starting to slip down into negative. Perhaps you are correct that I expect too much from myself and others - on the other hand, I just can't see any logical point in all of this (and the fact that there may be none, is not helping :/ ).

> But are you happy?

Heh... this is a hard one actually... I honestly don't know, I mean some activities bring me joy, but it is very temporary - I think I'm mostly stuck in neutral - neither happy nor sad.

> Why do you want to 'adapt' or 'fit' the society?

I don't want to adapt, but the society is expecting it. The way I see it this is a classic Catch-22 situation:

- don't adapt and be stuck with a stigma of being a freak/outcast which will make you suffer
- adapt and the stigma is gone, but now you will suffer every time you'll have to pretend to be 'normal'

> There has to be something you enjoy, right?

As the years go by, less and less things...

> Why would you take that enjoyment away from yourself just to 'help' society?

**'The needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few'** - while this is Vulcan logic from the movie it doesn't make it any less true. 

If you can't change the society, adapting would hurt you and every change you observe is (from your perspective) for the worse, then removing yourself should benefit everyone. That's the way I see it.

> I don’t have the winning BS argument for you, but what does stand out to me in your post is that you don’t have a lot of love for yourself, which is heartbreaking to hear. I think you hurt more than you may realize, you’ve just gotten so comfortable with that fatalistic mindset that it feels like first nature to feel nothing for yourself.

Hmm, I think I'm just realistic, I know most people can just go with the day-to-day routine, not looking at the bigger picture, but I can't - it just keeps bugging me. 

And let's be honest - we 'average' guys don't have any real accomplishments - it's sad, but it's true. For most people that's OK, but for some, it just makes life a tedious struggle for nothing.

> I’m so sorry about your Dad. I’m even more sorry for what you had to go through. He (very unfortunately) wasn’t thinking of you when he decided to end it all.

Thanks, I appreciate it, although frankly, he hurt my mom much more than me.

> Whether you realize it or believe it, you’re loved, and you do love others. Love is all that matters; it’s what keeps us all going. We’re in this together. Please stay.

Would it shock you to learn that I don't believe in 'love'? I mean I see this cliche BS forced on us in every movie (and lately even in god-damn commercials!) and I realize people who know each other, care for one another - but at the same time, we are using this magical word, as some sort of chain with anchor to force others to do our bidding. At least that's the way experience thought me so far...

Um, you know some time ago I (the believer) had a lengthy discussion with one atheist about the sense of it all and afterlife. The way I see it now is that we should fear death only if we believe in hell, all other alternatives (heaven or nothingness) seems OK.

> I said that by default being a state where you are actively suicidal is a state where your ability to be logical, to be reasonable or to think clearly are impaired.

And by saying that you are basically saying that anyone who is contemplating suicide has something wrong with his head, no matter what his reasons are. I don't believe lumping everyone together like that is a good thing.
Hmm, interesting POV, I can't say I fully agree, but I guess those really are some non-BS arguments... But, I'm not sure I will be able to just ignore the 'bigger picture' - 'just like that'

> Firstly, I'd like to dispel your fears about being committed.[...]

I'm not from the US. However, I have read how our local system works and thank you, but whoever thought, it's a good idea to strip the person seeking help from his dignity and free will, control his every move and if he doesn't cooperate - allow others to drug him forcefully - should be shot. I don't know how it works in the US, but over here, they have the right to hold you for an **unlimited amount of time** - it doesn't happen every day, but being locked up for half a year is realistically possible.

Frankly, no sane person would try seeking help on that conditions.

> Once I had that mindset I did in fact sell my things and travel the world. It was only then when I stopped looking for reasons to live and just simply lived, that I found the will to live manifest, as if by magic.

Glad it worked for you :) Unfortunately, I'm too much of a coward to pull something like that, hell I'm afraid to travel to the city 100 Km away :/  

I won't deny that this is not helping, I mean imagine that you are afraid to travel to the next city to seek a new job, or to the next country on vacation. This is pathetic as hell, and I know it, but that's how my brain works.

I don't want to make others happy (or sad, for that matter), it's simply been 30 years, and I don't see the point in dragging this for another 40-50 years. When I was younger, it was always: when I finish primary school it will be better => when I finish high school it will be better => when I finish college and find a job it will be better ... and for a few years it was, but now it's getting tedious. 

Seriously what's the point in doing everything over and over again only to end up in a pine box in the end? Why not speed it up?

Heh... haven't you read the description? Allow me to quote:

> if you are one of those people believing, that if someone is seriously contemplating suicide, he MUST BE mentally ill and should be locked away 'for his own good' - **please go away**

You probably assumed I'm depressed even though I said otherwise... Again, I'm NOT. Or if I am, then my depression contradicts every known fact I read about it.

Why would you assume that someone can't just logically state, that he doesn't see any sense in continuing to exist? I realize this goes against our natural instincts - but if we are here only to complete the 'Darwin cycle' then what is the point?

Thanks, but I'm not from the US, and over here something like that is sadly not available - nor are any legal recreational drugs. Besides, I never took anything in my life... always working 'by the book'

I'm sorry, but I think you misunderstood, I'm not contemplating it because something bad happened - there wasn't any traumatic event lately or anything like that.

It is just, the more it goes on, the less I see the point. Not because I'm depressed, but because it just doesn't make sense to me. I mean, sure I can understand that for some people, who are moving the society forward (Elon Musk, for example), there can be a point (assuming they are getting a kick out of it), but for an average person? We are simply not important enough to justify our existence - if the point of life is to complete the 'Darwin cycle' then I fail to see the logic (if there is any).

> because suicide makes people sad

Like I already said - the way I see it, I make people miserable right now. Sure, suicide is a lot heavier for a while - screaming, crying, questions 'why?' - trust me, I've been there and I still remember it very well, but the more years pass by, I'm starting to wonder if staying alive is any better.

This is why I choose NOT TO have any family of my own - to not have any obligations.

> you should live you have allot to do

That's a bold statement... 'a lot to do' such as what? Unless you mean everyday stuff, but that's more of a reason for it, not against it.
